newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mercedes plans service network in China.
newsitem.headline: Mercedes plans service network in China.

text.p: Helmut Werner, chairman of Germany's Mercedes-Benz, said the carmaker is in intensive discussions with the Chinese car industry with a view to expanding its network of service centres in China.
Speaking in an interview with the German newspaper Welt am Sonntag to be published on Sunday, Werner went on to say that its A-Class and V-Class cars should do well in the Chinese market.
Mercedes was planning production capacity of 60,000 vehicles and 100,00 engines annually for its Multi-Purpose Vehicle mini-van project, which it is developing with China Motor Corp.
Werner was optimistic that the project would be a success for both parties in the venture.

Regarding Mercedes' current position in Asia, Werner said high duties made local manufacturing a necessity, but that in many cases volumes in local markets meant it was not worthwhile to produce locally.

In an attempt to get around these problems, Werner said Mercedes' next move would be to start building cars from kits using locally-supplied components in Vietnam, later expanding to Indonesia, Thailand and Malaysia.
